clue.text: Spooner's avoiding marsupial trainer

indicators.note: Spooner's points to the Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: avoiding means shunning
a roo (kangaroo) is a marsupial, and roo sounds like rue

explanation.surface: Someone is steering clear of a pouched animal that coaches athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spooner's" means swap the opening sounds: say SHUNNING ROO and it becomes RUNNING SHOE. A trainer in Britain is a sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is British English for a sports shoe, the kind worn for running.

clue.text: French firm let out houses in Lille to the personnel at last

indicators.note: To house something is to hold it inside.

parts.note: To let out a flat is to rent it.
In French 'to the' is au, and Lille is a French city.

indicators.note: Takes only the final letter of 'personnel'.

parts.note: Last letter of personnel.

explanation.surface: A French company letting property in Lille to its own staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Lille' tells you to put 'to the' into French: AU. RENT then houses AU and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the carmaker founded by the Renault brothers near Paris is one of France's best-known companies.

clue.text: Dead ant — not filling for insectivore

parts.note: A dead limb is numb.
ANT with its middle letter N taken out.

explanation.surface: An insect-eater turning its nose up at a dead ant with no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbat is an Australian marsupial that feeds on termites, so the ant in the surface suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat eats termites almost exclusively, so it is an insectivore.

clue.text: Writer's one meaningful novel, reportedly you rejected

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement
rejected means that letter is thrown out of the fodder before the rearranging

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: An author's single significant book, it is said, was turned down by you.
explanation.walkthrough: With U (sounding like 'you', as 'reportedly' says) 'rejected' from MEANINGFUL, MEANINGFL is left; 'novel' rearranges it to ANFLEMING, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming was the British author who created the spy James Bond.

clue.text: Interest king in chat

indicators.note: The king's letter is placed in the middle of the word for chat.

parts.note: Gab is idle talk or chatter.
R is short for rex, Latin for king.

explanation.surface: A king taking an interest in a bit of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in 'How does that grab you?'
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something that grabs you catches your attention and appeals to you.

clue.text: House neighbouring bar's second address for patriarch

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house.
A bar is a line or stripe; 'bar's' makes it LINE'S, written LINES.
S is the abbreviation for second.

explanation.surface: A house next to a pub, with a second address for the head of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' tempts you to a pub, but it is a line; the 's makes it LINES. The patriarch is a church leader, not a family head.
explanation.definitionFit: Some patriarchs of Orthodox churches are addressed as 'Your Holiness'.

clue.text: Sooner clear the air having clashed, wanting composed chat

indicators.note: things that have clashed are jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the letters of chat are removed from the fodder
composed means put together anew, so the removed letters may come from anywhere in the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder
the letters taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: Better to settle a dispute sooner after a row, without calm conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting composed' C, H, A and T in any order, CLEAR THE AIR leaves LEREAIR, which 'having clashed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, so sooner in the sense of before now.

clue.text: Mortal wins heart of tyrannic deity

indicators.note: wins here means gains and holds, so the first word takes the other inside

parts.note: a human is a mortal

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: source of the middle letters

explanation.surface: A mere mortal triumphs over the core of a cruel god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of' tyrannic is AN, its middle two letters, which HUMAN 'wins' after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanuman is the monkey god of Hindu mythology, devoted ally of Rama.

clue.text: Learning to get used to residence outside university

parts.note: A habitation is a place of residence.
U is the abbreviation for university.

explanation.surface: A student learning to adjust to living off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase, read as a noun: the process of getting used to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Habituation is the process of becoming accustomed to something.

clue.text: Enticed Callum to strip, visibly embarrassed

indicators.note: Stripping peels off the outside, leaving the middle of 'Callum'.

parts.note: CALLUM with its outer letters C and M removed.
Someone visibly embarrassed goes red.

explanation.surface: Callum is coaxed into undressing and blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is one scene: Callum tempted to strip and red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to entice, so allured means enticed.

clue.text: Broadcast extremely groovy rhapsodic record of records

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order
extremely means take only the extreme letters, the first and last

parts.note: source of the outer letters
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A very cool, ecstatic radio show plays an old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' groovy gives GY; added to RHAPSODIC, 'Broadcast' scrambles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A discography is a catalogue of an artist's recordings, literally a list of their records.

clue.text: Dry January ultimately restricts everyone severely

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so these letters surround the next

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter

parts.note: source of the final letter
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Giving up drink after New Year's excess hems everybody in harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUT (very dry, of champagne) plus Y (January 'ultimately') 'restricts' ALL, holding it before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutally means harshly or cruelly, much the same as severely.

clue.text: Escapades of opponents carrying clubs

parts.note: Antis are people who are against something.
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards.

explanation.surface: Rivals getting up to mischief with golf or night clubs in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' is the card suit, abbreviated C.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name bouts of mischievous or reckless behaviour.

clue.text: Uprising soldiers arrested by gendarme, several merry

indicators.note: In a down clue, rising means reading bottom to top.

parts.note: Flic is French slang for a police officer, and a gendarme is one.
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers.
Several is some.

explanation.surface: A rebellion where several drunken soldiers are arrested by a French policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks like a revolt, but it tells you to turn OR upward to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone full of frolics, romping about, is in a merry mood.

clue.text: Symbol of clan is tailless bear

indicators.note: Cuts off the last letter.

parts.note: A totem is an emblem of a clan or tribe.

explanation.surface: A clan's emblem is a bear that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal on the totem, but it is the verb: to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: bear in its carrying sense, as in toting a bag or a gun.

clue.text: Pair's more organised having secured international promoter

indicators.note: Organising puts things in a new order, so the letters are rearranged.
The rearranged letters take in the I as well.

parts.note: Anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored.
I is the abbreviation for international.

explanation.surface: A couple, better organised, have signed up a promoter from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes into the mix before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and promotes shows and concerts.

clue.text: Rugby players showing impudence fight

parts.note: Front means cheek or nerve.
A row is a quarrel.

explanation.surface: Rugby players being cheeky and getting into a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the front row is the three forwards at the front of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The front row is the prop and hooker positions in a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Seemingly caught in trap, parent lying

indicators.note: The answer is caught inside the words that follow.

parts.note: The letters run from the end of 'trap' through 'parent' into the start of 'lying'.

explanation.surface: A parent, it seems, has been caught in a trap, lying there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parent' shows almost the whole answer on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both hedge a statement as how things appear, not how they surely are.

clue.text: Trialled set parts of various colours

parts.note: Pied means patched with different colours.
A lot at auction is a set of items.

explanation.surface: A multicoloured set tested out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like pieces of a set, but it is a verb: the colours word is parted to let the set in.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot a scheme is to trial it.

clue.text: Brown fish

definitions.meaning: A verb here: to scorch the outside of food until it browns.
A cold-water fish of the trout and salmon family.

explanation.surface: A brown fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' is a verb, as in browning meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Char means to scorch brown, and char is also a fish.

clue.text: Selfishly keep creative work, first for humorous satirist

parts.note: To hog is to keep for yourself.
Creative work is art.

indicators.note: Takes the first letter of 'humorous'.

parts.note: First letter of humorous.

explanation.surface: A satirist hoarding creative work, keen to be the first to be funny.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was the 18th-century English painter and engraver of satirical series such as A Rake's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth was a pictorial satirist of London life.

clue.text: Burdening to move, dropping wretched gun case

indicators.note: to move letters is to shift them about, so they are rearranged
dropping means the letters of gun are left out of the fodder
wretched means in a sorry state, so the dropped letters can come from anywhere in the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder
the letters dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: A load is lightened by getting rid of a dreadful firearm's holster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping wretched' G, U and N in any order from BURDENING leaves BRDENI, which 'to move' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder is a folder or cover for holding papers together, a kind of case.

clue.text: Delivering all over the place, not ever relaxing or being unoccupied

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
not means the letters of ever are excluded from the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder
the letters excluded from the fodder

explanation.surface: A courier making scattered drops never gets to rest or has nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' E, V, E and R, DELIVERING leaves DLIING, rearranged as 'all over the place' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Idling means doing nothing, whether lazing at ease or standing without work to do.

clue.text: Misbehaving dog about to bite fool from behind

indicators.note: from behind means read from the end, so the letters run backwards
to bite is to close the jaws on, so these letters grip the others

parts.note: a pug is a small dog breed
CA is circa, Latin for about
nit (nitwit) means a fool

explanation.surface: A dog that is set to nip an idiot from the rear is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: PUG and CA together are 'to bite' NIT, making PUGNITCA, which is read 'from behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting up is an idiom for behaving badly, especially of children or machines.

clue.text: Idiot forcibly hit bar close to you

indicators.note: To bar is to exclude, so the letter is kept out.

parts.note: To clout someone is to hit them hard.

indicators.note: The last letter of 'you'.

parts.note: Last letter of you, taken out of CLOUT.

explanation.surface: An idiot punching a barman near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a verb here, meaning leave out, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a British word for a fool.

clue.text: Normal after moulting, tarantula changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are reordered
a moulting creature sheds its outer layer, so the outside letters are dropped

parts.note: source of the inner letters

explanation.surface: It is quite usual for a big spider to look different once it has shed its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: TARANTULA 'after moulting' loses its outer T and A, leaving ARANTUL, and 'changed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means as expected or ordinary, a synonym for normal.

clue.text: Soldier's command US General verbalised

parts.note: A command is an order.
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general; the suffix -ly is said the same way.

explanation.surface: An American general issuing a spoken command to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Soldier stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly is a soldier who attends an officer.

clue.text: Realistic because of where we live

definitions.meaning: Describes a practical, sensible person without illusions.
'Down to' means because of, and Earth is where we live.

explanation.surface: Being realistic because of our home planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: something 'down to Earth' is owed to Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for realistic and practical, while the literal reading makes something owed to our planet.
